patterns: 1. Relay and chase work dominates human touches: of ~55 distinct human actions across the 10 cases, roughly 75-80% are pure message relays (quote to landlord, approval to contractor, invoice to landlord), reminder chasers or hold-status bookkeeping. Case 001 has 14 hold notes and 3 landlord chases in 62 days; case 008 has 7 landlord chasers (events 21-36) and case 009 has 7 near-identical tenant emails (events 1-17).

2. The slow stages are third-party silence, not work time. Contractor/landlord latency: 001 ev4-22 landlord quotes 23 days; 006 ev5-12 contractor quote 19 days despite 3+ reminders; 008 second quote 26 days and landlord decision 23 days; 005 ev4-10 8 days because the checkout report wasn't attached. Landlord approval itself is often fast when asked cleanly (002 3h; 006 1h; 007 next day; 004 same day), so the gap is quote collection and chasing, which an agent can parallelise (2-3 quotes at once on void properties) and escalate after 48h.

3. Data quality/wrong-recipient/wrong-document errors are systematic: wrong addresses in chasers (008 events 21,24,28,34,45; 009 events 11,16,17 - a cross-tenancy data leak risk), wrong attachment sent (008 ev6 checkout report instead of estimate), quote for another property (005 ev11), duplicate sends (004 ev23/26, 009 ev3/4, ev16/17), contractor/landlord names inconsistent, and attachment loss (002 invoice 'unavailable'). Date contradictions between inspection report dates and case dates appear in 003, 004, 005, 007, 008. A verification layer (address/job ID on every outbound and inbound document) would remove these.

4. Checkout/void jobs are mis-handled by system state: 'NOT TENANTED - moved to Paused' triggered manual intervention in 004, 005, 007, 008 (4 of 7 void cases); templates still say 'contact the tenant to arrange appointment' (006). Close-out is a click-through checklist ('Need confirmation from landlord' then closed within seconds: 003, 007, 008, 004) with photos routinely skipped ('No before and after photos' 004, 007, 008), weakening tenant deposit recharge claims. Cleaning quotes ranged GBP 90-205 and invoices were unitemised (003, 004), yet recharge to tenant was stated only once (004 ev10).

5. Money leakage and dependencies: 008 shows GBP 670 (49%) quote spread, GBP 180 invoice-vs-quote variance and an unpaid prior invoice causing the contractor to hesitate (ev39), 007 shows a GBP 1.63 net variance never reconciled, 003 invoice paid 43 days after sending, 008 landlord approval to pay 15 days after invoice. Dependency tracking (004: cleaning waited 13 days on separate checkout works) and recurring obligations (010: quarterly meter read held as a 74-day open ticket) are not modelled as first-class objects.

6. Tenant-facing cases are better served but state tracking suffers: 002 (blocked toilet) moved fast on dispatch (visit next day, landlord approved in 3h) but lost 4 days to missing contractor report and was re-opened by a dashboard bug after closure (ev44). Tenant-side delays are typically soft (009 medical hardship, 010 slow reply) - an agent should detect vulnerability and switch channel (SMS/upload link) rather than repeat email.

Approval and chase latency dominates the timeline. Approval/ack gaps (agency and landlord) are the largest single blocks in 8 of 10 cases: 011 (4.2d landlord + 2.6d to assign), 012 (4.6d to first contact), 016 (6.2d landlord, email in spam), 017 (2.6d first ack + 2d landlord), 018 (16d for contractor), 019 (13.8d + 10d landlord). Automated 3-day 'no response' flags (011 ev6, 016 ev5, 019 ev6) hand the ticket to a human, but the next real chase came 3-11 days later. An escalating SMS/phone chase at 24-48h plus an alternate contact would remove roughly 30-45% of elapsed days.

Many tickets are diagnostic or workaround problems, not repairs: 3 of 10 closed with no contractor spend and 1 with no repair work: 014 (key-latch workaround), 017 (hob switch), 016 (door 'settled'). A tenant triage step at intake (check switch, isolator, door seal) would resolve 017 on day 0; 012 added troubleshooting but landlord had already approved (ev8), costing ~6 days. Policy: triage first only when approval is not already on file.

Human touches are mostly mechanical: dispatching, relaying messages, holds and form-filling. Across the 10 cases roughly 65-70 of 75 logged human touches are judged 'yes' or 'partly' automatable; typical examples are 'Landlord approval confirmed' (ev10 in 011, ev10 in 016), the thank-you misread as approval (017 ev6), manual 'Change Mode' (015 ev12). The truly human items are small: spend approval for GBP 95-600 (011, 019), tenancy decisions (020 ev20), follow-up of an unsafe frame (014).

Data and communication errors recur and cost trust: wrong property in a landlord email (015 ev16, Flat 10 vs Flat 16), contradictory close-out message to landlord (016 ev24 'invoice was needed'), 'No issues' summary contradicting the attached report (020 ev17-18), contractor/tenant/staff names drifting in the same case (011, 012, 015, 016), unavailable attachments/invoice text in 8 of 10 cases, extraction failures at contractor replies (013 ev11, ev17; 016 ev21), a thank-you misclassified as approval (017), and a stray misrouted call after closure (013 ev35).

Money is lightly governed and often unverified: invoices are passed to landlords 'off the rent' without amounts (013 GBP 162.85, 015 GBP 68.97, 018 unstated, 019 deducted from rent after a quote of GBP 500+VAT and ~GBP 600 that are numerically identical once VAT is added). Work sometimes began before quote or approval (013 'I will proceed'; 019 approval logged after the work, ev32 vs ev31). The agent should state the VAT-inclusive total, enforce quote to approval to invoice reconciliation, and record who pays; in 011 a GBP 95 dial was approved while the tenant was told to fit it herself.

Closure is slow and untidy relative to resolution: 017 closed 4.7 days after the tenant confirmed it works; 013, 015, 018 closed 0-4 days after the invoice only; 019's holds were used as a status log (~15 hold events across 89 days); visit dates were missing in 015 and 018. Follow-up work is not created even when risks are flagged: 014 frame wobble, 015 door rot ('recommends modern replacement'), 018 tree/cables, 019 builders' waste disposal, 020 dog flap.

Most of the dwell time sits in the 'provider silence' gap, not in landlord approval: 024 (20 days, events 13-16), 025 (20 days, events 22-42, ~13 holds and 3 chasing calls), 029 (17 days, events 5-14), 030 (12 days to book + 3.9 days after a missed visit, events 8-39). Landlord approvals were usually answered in under 2 hours (021 ev 6, 023 ev 6, 026 ev 9, 030 ev 10), except for 028's silent landlord (13 days). Opportunity: an agent that chases contractors at 24-48h and reassigns after 3 reminders would compress the 4 slowest cases by roughly 10-17 days each.

The agency routinely does not know the job is finished: 023 (contractor had finished 26 Jul, chasers 27 Jul, event 17-20), 028 (landlord finished 19 Jun; agency learned on 3 Jul, event 12), 022 (finished 18-20 Nov, agency found out by phoning on 20 Nov, event 13), 030 (visit missed, found 3 days later, events 33-34). A 'confirm completion' check with contractor and tenant within 24h of the visit window would close 2-13 days earlier.

Data hygiene is poor and creates avoidable human touches: names of tenants/contractors/landlords change inside a single case (021 phone numbers, 022 cross-property call, 023 Theo/Freya, 025 Leo/Oliver, 026 Clara/Ruben/Grace/Harriet, 030 contractor under 8 names); dates are wrong or contradictory (025 'March 2025' in a 2024 case and 21 May/21 Jun/25 Jun, 026 30 Aug = Saturday labelled 'Monday', 030 20 Oct 2024 = Sunday labelled 'Monday'); attachments unavailable in 5 of 10 cases (021, 024, 025, 028, 030). An agent that normalises entities and validates calendar dates would eliminate whole classes of clarification calls.

Multi-issue and out-of-scope messages pollute cases and leave work orphaned: 024 (fence at ev 15, roof leak at ev 32, still open at closure), 027 (parking query inside a closed drain case, ev 11-16), 022 (another property's jobs in call summary, ev 13). The checklist also forces irrelevant steps ('Keys return confirmed' on oven, basin and balcony jobs: 024 ev 22-28, 029 ev 20-21, 023 ev 25-26) which add 1-6 days of idle state (029) or 4-7 state thrashes (024). Splitting into separate cases and tailoring closure checks per job type is cheap.

Money and responsibility are often undocumented: no invoice amount appears in any of the 10 cases (invoices mentioned in 022, 023, 024, 026, 030 but never parsed); 025 shows real cost leakage risk (installer first said out of warranty, a 2-year manufacturer warranty then covered it, saving the landlord an uncapped repair); 027 correctly allocates drain blockage to tenant; 029 leaves landlord vs tenant liability for a pre-existing cracked basin unresolved (deposit-dispute risk); 026 and 024 are move-in defects that landlords should bear. An agent that records liability reasoning and warranty checks early protects both the landlord and the tenant.

Tenant experience is mostly passive; tenants chased the agency in only 3 of 10 cases (026 ev 21 on date confusion, 028 ev 9 tenant emailed directly 'no one has acknowledged it yet', 024 ev 15 and 32 chasing fence and roof), but the agency rarely proactively updates tenants (025 oven out for ~1 month, 029 no tenant comms after day 0, 028 no closure message). Quick wins: same-day acknowledgement, status SMS at each handoff and a closure confirmation.

Approval and chasing latency dominate cycle time, not the work itself: median days_open is ~11 days (range 1-44), but physical repair needed 1 visit in 9/10 cases. Typical idle gaps: quote-to-landlord forwarding 3 days (032 ev12->18), landlord approval 0.1-3 days, contractor first contact 5-6 days after dispatch with 2-3 reminders needed (031 ev6->10, 037 ev11->15), invoice/completion note 2-3 days after visit (031, 039, 036). Roughly 50% of calendar time in each case is 'waiting for provider' with automated reminder emails only.

Cross-property contamination appears in 8 of 10 cases: wrong flat/address in landlord or closure emails (034 ev11, 037 ev23, 033 ev37), call summaries for other properties (032 ev32, 038 ev4, 039 ev15), plus person/provider name drift (Meadow Solutions/Harbour/Keystone in 031; Oliver/Rowan/Ruben/Freya). An agent must verify property/tenant identity against the case before sending anything or extracting a date/amount.

Date and extraction errors that a validator would catch: visit dates set in the past (032 ev13: 11/10 on 12/10; 033 ev14: 3 Oct on 4 Oct), 'May 1st' for an October job (032 ev32), Monday booked as Saturday (039 ev18), 'completed 17 April' for a July job (031 ev22), 3 vs 4 Nov appointment (036 ev39/41). Email extraction failed in 031 ev15, 034 ev9, 032 ev16; attachments (quotes, invoices, photos) unavailable in 8 of 10 cases so amounts are invisible, e.g. only 032 states a price (GBP 172.51 + VAT).

Closure and follow-through gaps: checklists say 'Need confirmation from landlord' then close within seconds (031 ev26-27, 034 ev15-16, 039 ev27-28); 040 closed 'no further action' despite promising an inspection and left the landlord to chase (ev13); 034 landlord paid 14 days after close; tenant confirmation that the fix works is almost never requested (034, 035, 037). Landlord-DIY and tenant-swap cases (035, 038, 040) were closed on a phone note without written record or inventory update.

Tenant-facing sentiment is mostly low-friction (7/10 no chase), but the single long case (036, 44 days) shows what happens when a provider owns a defect: 4 agency chases (ev23, 34, 48 + ev45 note), 2 tenant calls (ev28, 30), landlord complaint (ev43). Highest-value agent behaviours: auto-forward quote same day, 24h/48h provider escalation to a backup, date/identity validation, weekly status updates, outcome emails to landlord and tenant, and urgency triage ('leaking' 037, 031) to cut water-damage risk.

Human effort is mostly routine message drafting and state-juggling: of ~60 human touches logged across the 10 cases, roughly 70% are fully avoidable by an agent (templated emails, reminders, parsing of replies, date selection, 'review manually' prompts), ~25% partly (approvals, invoice checks, landlord phone calls), and under 5% not avoidable. The main irreducible human decisions are landlord approvals above a spend limit and accountability for a repeat-defect provider.

Idle agency time dominates: in 044 the agency spent about 26 of 32 days before the first landlord email (events 1-9); in 047 events 26-35 are 93 days of eight identical holds with no outbound message; in 045, 16 hold events cover 80 days. Time spent waiting on landlords is short (median reply under 1 day when asked clearly: 042 1h, 044 0.8d, 048 39min, 049 5min, 050 30min, 046 4h), so the main avoidable delay is the agency not asking, not the landlord not answering.

Contractor silence is the second driver: 047 (never responded to 3 emails + 3 SMS), 048 (6 days to first reminder), 043 (2.6 days), 046 (14-day booking gap), 045 (landlord's contractor, 48 days after quote). An agent that sets a 48h SLA and re-dispatches or alerts a second contractor would remove most of it.

Close-out is manual and error-prone: 6 of 10 cases show stale 'No work results'/'3+ reminders' alerts (042, 044, 046, 047, 048), failed extractions (046 e32, 050 e17 and e31), invoices in the wrong format (046, 050) or an alert firing after the work was already done (044 e20 after e19; 048 e21 after e16). Completion emails also name wrong properties (048 e16-17: Flat 7, 177 Beacon Close) and 045/047 reference several other flats.

Money is approved blind: 042, 044, 046, 048 and 050 had landlord approval with no cap or price, then the cost was disclosed after the work (042 e25 £75+VAT; 048 quote added after work; 050 landlord told £49.40 inc VAT vs quoted £35/£90+VAT). Cost leakage is small per case (£35-£108) but unreconciled in every one.

Landlord-managed jobs (041, 045, 047) are the worst for visibility: 80, 111 and 13 days, agency blind, closed 'without payment' on a one-line landlord email, with no tenant confirmation. These are the two longest cases (045, 047) and in both no outbound tenant update is logged after the first weeks.

Data hygiene problems repeat: inconsistent tenant, landlord and contractor names in 8 of 10 cases, dispatch email duplicates (050 e14-15, 043 e10-11), key-return gate on non-key jobs (043, 044, 046, 048), and intake templates that ask irrelevant questions (042 boiler make for a washing machine; 049 ceiling sagging for a shed door).
